newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee pushed down by late dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee pushed down by late dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed lower on late commercial demand for dollars, with some banks also buying the U.S. currency from the Central Bank, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.81 to the dollar, after opening at 57.80. The rupee closed at 57.74 on Wednesday.
Although the dollar-rupee rate went to 57.77 in the morning, banks were unable to cover imports early due to a lack of substantial volumes at less than 57.80, dealers said.
"The rupee fell only on import covering demand for dollars. Speculators were absent since the exchange rate was so close to the Central Bank's top level," said a Panasia Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by one local cent, and fixed buying and selling prices at 56.6750 and 57.8200.
"Some banks also bought dollars from the Central Bank, to cover imports," said the Panasia dealer.
Overnight call money closed at 13 percent with the market well offered.
"Banks buying dollars from the Central Bank on one day will not have an impact on the money market, which is very liquid," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
